description: We are The Build Club, a team of passionate builders interested in AI, software, SaaS, and problem-solving. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we aim to create an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that makes space exploration engaging and educational. We welcome curious minds with skills in AI/ML, web development, game development, UI/UX, astronomy, data analysis, and space science. Let's learn, build, and explore together!

Designed to make space exploration engaging and educational, the game challenges players to explore their habitat, respond to critical emergencies, and make decisions that affect crew safety and mission success.

Through interactive missions, realistic Mars environments, physics-based movement, and science-inspired scenarios, players discover the challenges of living and working on Mars. The experience incorporates NASA space-weather information through the DONKI API, with clearly identified archived fallback data when live information is unavailable.

Our goal is to turn complex space-safety concepts into an accessible, memorable learning experience that inspires the next generation of explorers.
details:
SOL COMMANDER: Last Habitat

Project Overview

SOL COMMANDER: Last Habitat is a browser-based 3D Mars adventure and astronaut mission-training experience. Players take on the role of Commander Nova, leading a crew of four astronauts stationed at a remote Martian outpost.

Our goal is to make the challenges of human exploration on Mars engaging and understandable through interactive gameplay. Instead of simply reading about space exploration, players experience a Martian environment, explore their habitat, interact with their surroundings, and respond to critical mission emergencies.

How It Works

The experience takes players through an 88-Sol campaign on Mars. As Commander Nova, players explore a fully interactive 3D outpost, encounter five critical emergency scenarios, and make decisions that influence mission operations and crew safety.

The game also includes a Free-Roam mode, allowing players to continue exploring the Martian environment beyond the main missions. A rover companion named Rusty follows the player and performs movement and yielding behaviours within the environment.

NASA Data and Scientific Foundation

SOL COMMANDER incorporates NASA's DONKI (Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information) Space Weather API to retrieve space-weather information, including solar flares, solar energetic particles, and coronal mass ejections.

When live information is unavailable, the experience uses clearly labelled archived fallback data rather than presenting old information as live updates.

The Martian environment is also informed by NASA's Mars Fact Sheet, including Mars' surface gravity, atmospheric density, and solar irradiance. Scientific research on the Perseverance rover's SuperCam microphone and the Martian soundscape further informed our understanding of the environment.

Technology and Development

The project was developed as a web-based application using React 19, TypeScript, Three.js, Vite, and Rapier3D WASM physics.

Three.js powers the interactive 3D environment, while Rapier provides physics-based movement and collision detection. Procedurally generated environments, textures, and Web Audio sound effects help create an immersive experience without relying on large collections of external 3D assets.

The application runs directly in a web browser, making the experience easier to access without requiring a separate game installation.

Educational Impact

Our aim is to inspire curiosity about planetary science, engineering, and the challenges of human space exploration.

By placing players in the role of a mission commander, SOL COMMANDER encourages exploration, observation, problem-solving, and safety-focused decision-making. It transforms space-related concepts into an interactive experience that can help young learners better imagine what it takes to live and work on Mars.

Innovation

SOL COMMANDER combines browser-based 3D exploration, physics-based gameplay, mission emergencies, a companion rover, and NASA space-weather information in one educational experience.

Rather than presenting Mars exploration as static educational content, the project lets players experience a simulated mission environment and learn through interaction.

AI Transparency and Credits

AI tools, including Google Gemini, Google AI Studio, and Google Antigravity, supported parts of the development process through coding assistance, debugging, and visual asset creation. AI-generated project visuals include the game's icon and logo.

AI assistance and generated assets are disclosed in the project's documentation and credits. The game does not use AI-generated character voices; its sound effects are created using procedural Web Audio.

Project Links

Live Game: https://solcommander.brokentube.cloud

Source Code: https://github.com/brokentube45/sol-commander

SOL COMMANDER: Last Habitat is an independent educational project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by NASA.
